explanations: The refund route checks the caller's role and scope but then loads the payment with findById, which is not scoped to the caller's account. Every other route uses a findByIdForAccount lookup so that records from other accounts look like 404s. Any billing_admin in tenant A who knows or guesses a payment ID from tenant B can issue a refund against it (an insecure direct object reference / broken object-level authorization). The lookup should be payments.findByIdForAccount(req.params.paymentId, req.auth!.accountId).

Both middlewares must pass. requireRole("billing_admin") succeeds, then requireScope("refunds:write") fails with 403 insufficient_scope; the handler never runs. 401 is only returned when no valid identity is present, and the lookup is never reached.

findByIdForAccount returns null both when the ID does not exist and when it belongs to a different account, so the route cannot distinguish them and responds 404 to both. That prevents ID enumeration across tenants. Returning 403 would be the option that leaks existence.

The invoice routes are guarded only by requireScope("invoices:read"), which the token satisfies. GET /payments/:id requires the support or billing_admin role, so a viewer gets 403, and the refund route requires billing_admin plus the refunds:write scope. Matching the account does not bypass role checks.
